{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABYxno1w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhCW-I4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 45, "title": "Make the terminal the sole interactive interface for PC-VAN, including handles, posts, replies and settings", "body": "## Problem

The current PC-VAN looks like a late-1990s text service, but many ordinary operations abruptly escape into modern browser forms and helper UI: `WRITE` and `REPLY` open a modal editor, reading a reply exposes a clickable “返信先 RE#... を読む” helper link under the terminal, user registration/selection happens inside Settings, and much of setup/AI/storage is controlled through buttons, select elements and dialogs. This breaks the central experience. Real text-service interaction was operated through the **terminal input and its own screen prompts**; this project should prioritize the *experience of operating it*, rather than merely drawing a historical-looking menu.

The user specifically requests **no app-created dialogs, helper links, floating panels or extra action buttons for normal operation**. Every operation the application offers should be reachable and completable from the same text terminal command entry, including first-time handle setup and writing multi-line messages.

This must be a working migration of the interaction model, **not** hiding the existing controls and losing functionality.

## Expected outcome

**One primary interface: PC-VAN transcript + a persistent terminal input.** Menus, registration, navigation, article reading, thread replies, post composition/edit/review/submit/cancel, local preferences, AI model preparation and controls, backup/import, and factory reset all work through conversational command prompts and keyboard input inside the terminal.

Use a small, consistent, screen-aware command/prompt state machine: in a compose flow, the same input interprets a title or body line rather than a MAIN selector; in a confirmation flow it accepts only the advertised responses. Commands such as `HELP`, `BACK`, `MAIN` and `READ n` should behave predictably in their respective contexts. When an operation genuinely requires a browser-native capability (e.g. system file picker or download), it may be **initiated from a typed command**; avoid a custom modal/side panel.

Illustrative Japanese terminal interaction (proposed helper syntax, **not a claim of evidenced 1996 PC-VAN commands**):

```text
PC-VANへようこそ
ハンドル名を登録しますか？ (Y/N)=Y
ハンドル名=たか
登録しました。

MAIN
...
番号またはコマンド=J MITI
コマンド=3
コマンド=9
コマンド=WRITE

新規発言
タイトル=昔のパソコン通信
本文を入力してください（.END で終了 / .CANCEL で中止）
あの頃、夜更かしして通信していました。
いろいろな人の書き込みを読むのが楽しみでした。
.END

タイトル：昔のパソコン通信
本文：2行
投稿しますか？ (Y/N/EDIT)=Y
発言 #31 を登録しました。

コマンド=READ 32
...
返信先：#31
コマンド=READ 31
```

Preserve the original verified `J MITI → 3 → 9` route, MAIN menu entry labels, seeded conversations and existing browsing semantics.

## Context

Reinspect latest `main` before implementation. Relevant current modules:

- `src/terminal.ts`: one-line `#command` form already supports Enter/IME safety, command history, progressive rendering and screen-reader output. It also renders `.reply-reference` clickable link, `.open-settings`, `.reveal-output`, `.skip-connection`, `.download-log`, submit button, display sliders/selects and keyboard-help panel.
- `src/main.ts`: controller/queue orchestrates screen commands, `WRITE`/`REPLY` interception, read tracking, composer/Settings/AI/storage wiring, reconnect/activity, reset and cross-tab events. Keep asynchronous persistence and pending operation protection; do not fork separate systems for terminal vs UI.
- `src/composer.ts`: separate `.member-controls` user-registration form and `dialog`-based compose/review/send/cancel lifecycle. Reuse existing validated `LocalRepository.createHumanMember`, active-member setting and `createForumPost` instead of replacing storage semantics.
- `src/navigation.ts`, `src/connection.ts`: reconstructed command-scoped screen navigation, forum LIST/READ/HELP/BACK/MAIN and first-connection UX. Preserve the data-driven MAIN, SIG and empty-section functionality.
- `src/settings.ts`: Settings modal collects display, member, AI, storage, offline and help panels. Replace its action flows with terminal-native commands/screens, keeping About/provenance inspectable **on demand**.
- `src/ai/setup.ts`, `src/ai/controls.ts`: terminal-adjacent model banner, a browser consent dialog, model/profile selection, local generation/preview, activity and provenance controls. Preserve **explicit, informed consent** before a potentially GB-size WebLLM download, model/cross-tab leases, cancellation, progress, error states and automatic ten-resident scheduling. The prompt/disclosure and affirmative typed confirmation should be part of the terminal itself.
- `src/storage/controls.ts`, `src/offline/controls.ts`: JSON backup/import, offline/cache operations and the new `初期状態に戻す` (#43) are currently button/dialog-driven. Preserve atomic reset/restore, stale-world protections, optional offline caching and true backup functionality.
- `src/storage/repository.ts` and `src/storage/schema.ts`: authoritative IndexedDB data model; existing human posts, 30 initial seed posts, ten resident profiles and their generated posts, read states, per-world setup consent, session history and JSON backups must not be lost.
- `src/output-renderer.ts`, `src/history.ts`, current browser tests: avoid regressions to byte-paced rendering, skip, focus, IME, accessibility, persistence and background AI simulation.
- Development conventions: [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md). Issue/PR/docs authored in English; product and terminal text in Japanese.

### Design expectations

1. **First-time handle flow:** On a new local world, after connection and without leaving the terminal, invite the visitor to choose a handle (and allow `N` or `SKIP` so reading is never blocked). Once registered, subsequent sessions remember the selection. A user without a handle who enters `WRITE`/`REPLY` should be guided into the inline registration flow and then returned to their pending post intent. Provide a terminal command to display/change/select a stored human handle, without confusing the ten fictional regulars with selectable human accounts. Keep per-user read states.
2. **Post composer as a terminal state machine:** `WRITE` and `REPLY n` first check the destination and selected human identity, then show title prompt, successive body lines, an unambiguous end-of-body sentinel (e.g. `.END`), a clear preview/confirmation, and an actual save. Support cancel at every step, editing title/body after preview (e.g. `EDIT` and line-based replacement/delete commands), exact preservation of multiline Japanese text, empty/length validation with non-destructive errors, safe reply parent integrity, and no duplicate sends. Commands during drafting must not accidentally navigate MAIN or post. Invalid and interrupted states must recover predictably.
3. **Read/reply solely by commands:** `READ n` shows title, body and an ordinary `返信先：#m` reference when present. The user types `READ m` or `REPLY n`; do not render a “read referenced post” link, clickable action, or separate navigation helper. Keep LIST and unread markers.
4. **Terminal-native operations throughout:** Provide discoverable command menus such as `SETTINGS`/`CONFIG` (display theme/speed, session details, handle selection, AI model/automatic activity/profile editing, storage and offline tasks), `ABOUT`, `HELP`, log export, JSON backup/restore and `RESET`. Keep their status, progress and warnings inside the transcript. Avoid introducing dozens of hard-to-memorize flat commands: hierarchical numbered menus and short documented aliases are suitable. The app must not leave a major previously supported operation accessible *only* through a hidden form.
5. **Important confirmation boundaries:** A heavy model download, replacing local data via import, and destructive reset require a deliberate, plainly worded, typed affirmative response that is verified in the correct active operation context. No accidental authorization by `Enter` on an empty prompt or default-ON activity. Browser-native file selection and saving are allowed **only as a consequence of a typed action**; the user should return to terminal input afterward. External permission UI invoked by browser security APIs is not an app-created modal and cannot be suppressed.
6. **Unobtrusive presentation:** In the PC-VAN world do not advertise “AI住人,” “fictional generation,” source links or simulator explanations at every interaction. On-demand ABOUT/provenance and consent messages must still honestly explain local-only simulation and artificial content. Preserve current nontechnical author handles in ordinary messages.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] The terminal transcript and command input are the **only interactive app-specific surface** for normal navigation, registration, composing, replying, settings/preferences, model loading/consent, AI management, backups/import, reset, offline options and help. Remove/rework app-created dialogs, floating AI invitation/action strip, reply-reference anchor, helper buttons and Settings click panels, without disabling their functionality. Unavoidable OS/browser-native file selection/download/permission interfaces are permitted **only** when triggered by a terminal command.
- [ ] On first use, an in-terminal, optional handle-registration flow is offered (skip possible). Registration, changing/selecting a handle, and the unregistered user's `WRITE`/`REPLY` handoff require no modal. After creating a handle during a posting attempt, resume that intent safely. Existing human identities, current selection, per-human read markers and backup semantics persist across reloads.
- [ ] `WRITE` creates a title/body draft and `REPLY n` binds the correct local parent, entirely through one terminal input. Multiline text, Japanese IME composition, editing before send, preview, explicit Y/N confirmation, error recovery, cancellation and successful transactional post saving work end-to-end; no input submits merely because an IME conversion is confirmed. Retried operations do not create duplicate posts. A cancelled draft must never become a stored post.
- [ ] `READ n` and LIST continue to work for the seeded human/AI conversations and new posts; reply parent numbers appear in plain text, with **no clickable “返信先を読む” UI**. Reading and replying by typing commands works without a mouse; existing SIG routes, MAIN 1–21/X, navigation, empty views and Q/RECONNECT remain intact.
- [ ] A documented, screen-aware `SETTINGS` (or equivalently named) terminal menu covers **all** formerly actionable display/theme/speed/preferences, handle selection, AI model selection/setup, resident activity and profile editing, generation preview/save, data export/import, local-world factory reset, offline cache/storage and log export. The command-only migration must retain real underlying actions, not just text placeholders. A typed `HELP` shows available commands for the current context and an easy return path.
- [ ] Heavy model download requires an explicit in-terminal consent explanation and user-entered approval; refusal/invalid commands/no input never authorize or download. Progress, model stop/error/ready states, new-world default auto activity, independent resident scheduling, cross-tab coordination and the recent fictional posts remain unchanged. Technical provenance stays accessible through `ABOUT`/details, not regular forum output.
- [ ] `BACK`, `MAIN`, cancel and help have deterministic behavior throughout nested menus, first-run setup, draft editing and confirmation; they must never silently discard a draft or confirm a destructive operation. Handle stale pending async work, reset/restore, another tab, storage failures, disconnect/reconnect and repeated input without interleaving prompts or committing to an outdated world.
- [ ] Maintain output streaming and skip-by-Escape (or a clearly documented terminal shortcut), history up/down, transcript scroll, responsive full-screen terminal, literal text rendering and safe focus. Accessibility includes a usable input label, clear prompts/state changes in the log, keyboard/screen-reader support and Japanese IME. Any hidden non-interactive semantic helpers are fine; no visible secondary command UI.
- [ ] Keep historical research and evidence boundaries: terminal convenience commands are documented as reconstructed interactions, not falsely verified original PC-VAN sequences. Keep fictional AI/seed provenance and local-only limitations inspectable without immersion-breaking default text.
- [ ] Add controller/state-machine and browser E2E tests that complete *first run → handle registration → read seeded post → REPLY/WRITE line by line → preview/edit → confirm → LIST/READ → reload*, all without clicking application buttons or opening dialogs. Also verify skip/cancel, malformed/blank bodies, IME, saved content, read tracking, model-consent refusal/acceptance, backup/import and reset confirmation, parallel-tab interruptions, and absence of unsolicited modal/helper UI. Mock WebLLM and system file pickers where needed; no real GPU/download required.
- [ ] Update README, command help, accessibility guidance and AI/storage documentation to list actual working terminal commands and the screen-aware editing/consent sequences. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and applicable focused checks, and report actual results.

## Optional validation

A manual keyboard-only walkthrough on desktop and mobile, including Japanese IME and line-by-line composition, is valuable for judging the authentic PC-VAN experience, but is not a required pre-merge subjective gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None required: command flows, browser interactions and storage operations can be tested before merge against the production build. GitHub Pages publication is an independent deployment workflow.
